claims.text: The starting material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
A thin, dense Al2O3 coating should be applied to the alloy surface, for example by chemical vapor deposition.
The applied Al2O3 coating will be continuous and adherent.
A continuous Al2O3 surface layer acts as a diffusion barrier.
The Al2O3 coating restricts oxygen diffusion into the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Restricting oxygen diffusion prevents deep oxidation or pesting.
Applying the coating only at the surface preserves the beneficial bulk microstructure.
Relative to uncoated material, alumina-coated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will have significantly lower oxygen uptake during exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
Alumina-coated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will show no severe surface oxidation after exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
Alumina-coated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will show no severe subsurface oxidation after exposure to air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
The coating will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to untreated material.
The coating will preserve yield strength at approximately 1000 °C relative to untreated material.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation or pesting in high-temperature air.
The proposed protection is bounded to short exposures of about 5 hours in air near 800 °C without significant external mechanical loading.
Protection during much longer exposures or under high strain rates has not been established.
Long-term coating adhesion and stability and coating behavior under variable loading are uncertain.
